title: Sicut erat in principio
readingOutcome: Recognize ongoing/background past action and narrative adverbs.

casePanel.policy: All six cases remain active; tense work does not replace case retrieval.

imperfectFramework.readingValue: ongoing, repeated or background past action/state

learnerCopy.en: The imperfect presents an action or state as ongoing, repeated or background in the past. It is the tense of 'was', 'was doing', 'used to do' and similar narrative setting.
learnerCopy.fr: L'imparfait présente une action ou un état comme continu, répété ou en arrière-plan dans le passé. C'est le temps de « était », « faisait », « avait l'habitude de » et de la mise en scène narrative.

learnerCopy.en: The imperfect of sum is eram, eras, erat, eramus, eratis, erant. In Sicut erat in principio and the Last Gospel, erat is background description: 'was'.
learnerCopy.fr: L'imparfait de sum est eram, eras, erat, eramus, eratis, erant. Dans Sicut erat in principio et le dernier Évangile, erat décrit l'arrière-plan : « était ».

learnerCopy.en: Regular imperfects are highly visible: -bam, -bas, -bat, -bamus, -batis, -bant, with predictable variations such as -ebam and -iebam. Read the tense signal before translating the entire clause.
learnerCopy.fr: Les imparfaits réguliers sont très visibles : -bam, -bas, -bat, -bamus, -batis, -bant, avec des variantes prévisibles comme -ebam et -iebam. Repérez d'abord le signal temporel.

learnerCopy.en: Three occurrences of erat describe a state rather than a completed event. This is exactly the narrative function the imperfect is meant to signal.
learnerCopy.fr: Trois occurrences de erat décrivent un état plutôt qu'un événement achevé. C'est précisément la fonction narrative signalée par l'imparfait.

learnerCopy.en: stabant is the imperfect of sto: 'they were standing'. autem connects the scene. The verb supplies background while the later narrative can move on to completed events.
learnerCopy.fr: stabant est l'imparfait de sto : « ils se tenaient debout ». autem relie la scène. Le verbe pose l'arrière-plan avant les événements achevés.

learnerCopy.en: tunc, ibi, adhuc, iam, statim and simul tell you when or how events relate. Treat them as navigation words: then, there, still, already/now, immediately, together.
learnerCopy.fr: tunc, ibi, adhuc, iam, statim et simul orientent le récit : alors, là, encore, déjà/maintenant, aussitôt, ensemble.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

translation.en: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
translation.fr: Comme il était au commencement, maintenant et toujours, et dans les siècles des siècles. Amen.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.

translation.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
translation.fr: Au commencement était le Verbe, et le Verbe était auprès de Dieu, et le Verbe était Dieu.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: In ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hominum.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: In ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hominum.

translation.en: In Him was life, and the life was the light of men.
translation.fr: En lui était la vie, et la vie était la lumière des hommes.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Stabant autem juxta crucem Jesu mater ejus.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Stabant autem juxta crucem Jesu mater ejus.

translation.en: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus His mother.
translation.fr: Près de la croix de Jésus se tenait sa mère.

exercises.hint: It is the past of sum used for background.
exercises.explanation: erat is third-person singular imperfect of sum.

exercises.prompt: What does the imperfect usually contribute to a narrative?
exercises.explanation: The imperfect frames ongoing, repeated or background past action/state.

exercises.prompt: Select every imperfect form of sum.
exercises.stimulus: In principio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
exercises.hint: The same form occurs three times.
exercises.explanation: All three erat forms are imperfect.

exercises.prompt: What does stabant mean in context?
exercises.stimulus: Stabant autem juxta crucem Jesu mater ejus.
exercises.explanation: stabant is third-person plural imperfect of sto.

exercises.prompt: Match the narrative adverb to its meaning.
exercises.hint: These orient time and place in narrative.
exercises.explanation: Narrative adverbs help segment Gospel clauses.

exercises.prompt: Match the connector/adverb to its meaning.
exercises.hint: These are structural words rather than content nouns.

exercises.prompt: Which form is first-person singular imperfect of sum?
exercises.hint: The paradigm begins eram, eras, erat.
It gives English 'sper-' words only indirectly.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'together / at the same time'?
exercises.explanation: simul means together / at the same time.

exercises.prompt: Give the Latin adverb meaning 'already / now'.
exercises.hint: It is a short narrative time word.

objectives: Recognize the imperfect as ongoing/background past.
Read erat and regular -ba- imperfect patterns.
Learn the fourteen frozen Lesson 11 lemmas.
Use narrative adverbs/connectors to orient a liturgical Gospel clause.
